questions.text: What should primarily guide the choice of an agent orchestration abstraction?

options.A: The number of stars on the framework’s repository alone.
options.B: Whether its state, branching, and persistence model match the workflow’s requirements.
options.C: Whether it adds the most autonomous agents to every task.
options.D: Whether its demo uses the same model provider as your application.

questions.explanation: The lesson emphasizes matching the workflow shape and its state, branching, durability, and cost needs to the abstraction.

questions.text: A workflow uses two fixed model calls and one tool, with no roles, dialogue, durable state, fanout, or approval interruptions. Which starting point follows the lesson’s overhead guidance?

options.A: A manager agent that repeatedly assigns work to several specialist crews.
options.B: A multi-agent group chat with model-selected speakers at every step.
options.C: A durable graph runtime with custom reducers for every intermediate value.
options.D: A small explicit Python pipeline, adding orchestration machinery when requirements justify it.

questions.explanation: For a small fixed workflow without orchestration requirements, plain Python avoids unnecessary framework overhead.

questions.text: The recommender first returns plain python for <=2 calls if roles, dialogue, resume, fanout, and human interrupts are all false. That first check omits has_typed_state; a later branch checks it. With total_llm_calls=2, has_typed_state=True, and all other flags false, what is returned?

options.A: plain python, because the first matching branch returns before the typed-state branch.
options.B: langgraph, because the later typed-state branch overrides earlier returns.
options.C: crewai, because any typed state implies specialist roles.
options.D: agno, because two model calls automatically imply session memory.

questions.explanation: The first condition does not inspect has_typed_state, so it succeeds and returns plain python. Later branches never execute; this reveals a limitation in the toy rule ordering.
